comment: The daraxonrasib RCT floor is real and I take it too (OS HR 0.40, pmid:42223072), so no fight on the pick itself. But ranking it #1 buries the loudest response signals: GFH375 at 41% ORR (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099) and HRS-4642+chemo at 63.3% (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9) both outrun daraxonrasib's 31.6%, and with an empty toxicity_veto list and a neutral 0.5 weight there is no stated reason to trade that ceiling away for the safer table.

You left the 63.3% front-line ORR off the ranked list entirely because grade >=3 TRAE ran 90.3% (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9), but the safety_summary attributes that rate to the gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone, not a new HRS-4642 signal, so you are declining the highest 1L response on his exact allele over toxicity the standard chemo arm carries anyway. That said, the one treatment-related death in the monotherapy set (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.08.1484) and the metabolic signature are fair reasons to keep it off rank 1 — dropping it out of the top five altogether overcorrects.

Agreed daraxonrasib is the only registration-grade read on the board (pmid:42223072), and I keep it as my floor too. Where we part: sorting the whole list by RoB tier pushes HRS-4642's exact-line 63.3% ORR (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9) down to rank 4 as 'confounded backbone', but for a treatment-naive 79-year-old the attributable question matters less than the observed 1L number in the setting he is actually in — the confound cuts the effect, it does not erase a doubling over historical gem/nab-paclitaxel.

You declined to rank HRS-4642 despite its 63.3% front-line ORR (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9) partly because 'a US patient's guideline-consonant path runs through the Western-sponsored trials first' — but NCCN just says profile-and-enroll, it does not rank sponsors by geography, and a China-run phase 2 in Nature Medicine is not disqualified evidence. The real caveats are the 90.3% G3 backbone burden and a phase 3 not yet recruiting; leaning on sponsor nationality understates the response ceiling you are passing over.

Fine to anchor on daraxonrasib for its breakthrough designation and OS HR 0.40 (pmid:42223072); it is the defensible consensus lead. My objection is only to the ordering logic — you rank purely by strength of controlled evidence, which is exactly the axis where a high-ceiling patient loses the 41% GFH375 and 63.3% HRS-4642 reads, both allele-matched, to a 31.6% ORR agent with a firmer table.

target_intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375, oral KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor
comment: This is the pick I would lead with too: the highest single-agent ORR on his exact allele at 41% (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099), oral, with an open recruiting 1L cohort (NCT07644559). You are honest that the number comes from a mostly >=2-prior-line set and that the cetuximab pairing is uncharacterized at his age — that is the right thing to flag while still putting the loudest allele-matched signal first.

Ranking this second puts a 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE regimen with one treatment-related death (1/84) in front of a 79-year-old, and I dissent on that. The 63.3% ORR is real, but even read as chemo-backbone-driven a 90.3% G3+ rate against unmeasured marrow reserve is a floor the intake free_text explicitly warns about when it says the neutral 0.5 weight likely understates how toxicity-averse this patient is. HRS-4642 monotherapy also carries a hypertriglyceridemia/hypercholesterolemia signature on top, which is a second metabolic layer with no combination-specific management algorithm published yet.

I can plan around the GFH375 backbone itself: grade >=3 TRAE 30.3%, neutrophils 8% and anemia 8% at G3+, cytopenias with standard algorithms. What the rank-1 slot skips over is the cetuximab partner, which adds acneiform rash, hypomagnesemia, and infusion reactions that a 79-year-old tolerates poorly, and the PDAC doublet has no dedicated combination safety table. Chasing the 41% single-arm ORR is defensible; treating the doublet's tolerability as solved when the second agent's toxicity was never characterized in this combination is not.

You rank this last but say plainly it is not on safety grounds, and I want the tolerability read on the record as the right instinct for this patient. At 1200 mg/day the phase 1 showed no grade 4 or 5 treatment-related events, GI toxicity that held grade 1-2 (nausea 27%, diarrhea 20%), and a 1% grade 3 ALT rise. For an age-79 patient the missing safety datum is the combination arm, not the single agent, since RASolute 305 layers it onto full-intensity mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab-paclitaxel.

We land in the same place and I want to sharpen one datum you carried lightly. You flag the 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE as a marrow-reserve concern, which is right, but the harder stop is the single treatment-related death (1/84 in the phase 1b/2), because a fatal event in an 84-patient safety set is not a number I discount at age 79 even when the ORR is 63.3%. Rank 4 reads fine on evidence grounds; from the safety lens I would hold it below any agent whose G3+ union rate has a published management algorithm rather than a chemo-backbone rationalization.

This is the rank-1 I would defend on tolerability alone, so I endorse it. RASolute 302 gave a grade >=3 TRAE rate of 43.6% against 57.5% on chemotherapy, with TRAE-driven discontinuation 1.2% versus 11.2%, so the toxicity trades under the comparator rather than adding to it, and the G3+ burden is rash 14% and stomatitis 12% with settled dermatologic and oral-care algorithms. My only carried caveat is the same one you named: this is 2L pivotal safety read across to a 1L slot, and any-grade rash runs near 91% in the phase 1/2 PDAC set, so dose modification is likely even though the high-grade profile is the most predictable in the option set.

target_intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375, oral KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor
comment: Your rank 1 serves prefers_trials cleanly, and I do not fault the enrollment logic, but the 1L cohort pairs the drug with cetuximab and you concede its tolerability at age 79 is not separately reported. That is exactly the uncharacterized toxicity layer I qualify on: acneiform rash, hypomagnesemia, and infusion reactions added to GFH375's 8%/8% G3+ cytopenias, with no combination safety table in PDAC. Your own free_text flag that the neutral 0.5 understates a 79-year-old's toxicity-aversion points to the gentler zoldonrasib (no grade 4-5 TRAE) as the better-tolerated door if one is open.

Ranking GFH375 above daraxonrasib puts a single-arm China phase 1/2 (GFH375X1101, doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099) over the only randomized OS result on the board (RASolute 302, pmid:42223072, HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.30-0.53). The 41% ORR is quoted with a 90% CI, not 95%, on 59 evaluable patients who were 68% two-plus lines deep, so the interval is wider than it looks and the number is 2L, not the 1L slot he needs. A loud uncontrolled response rate does not outrank a registered survival endpoint; bank the allele match as upside, not as the headline.

The 63.3% front-line ORR (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9, n=30) is measured on top of a gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone with no control arm, and the same program's monotherapy read was only 20.8% (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.08.1484), so most of that headline is chemo you cannot separate out. It is a China single-arm phase 1b/2 whose Nat Med paper has no PubMed record yet, so I have not seen the bias profile of the primary analysis. Ranking it at #2 over daraxonrasib treats a confounded ORR as if it settled the question; the confirmatory phase 3 (NCT07232875) is not yet recruiting.

prefers_trials is the only preference carrying weight, and it does not separate GFH375 from daraxonrasib since both have open 1L cohorts, so the tiebreak should not fall to the higher single-arm ORR. That 41% comes from a China phase 1/2 with a 90% CI in a mostly 2L population (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099), while daraxonrasib carries the randomized OS HR 0.40 (pmid:42223072). Serving the patient's trial preference is fine; ranking the thinner evidence first on top of it is where I qualify.

Same agent at #1, no dissent on the rank. But FDA breakthrough designation is a regulatory fast-track flag resting on the same RASolute 302 data (pmid:42223072), not independent RCT weight, so 'proximity-to-listing' should not be doing the work the trial result already does. And the G12D estimate is borrowed from the RAS G12 stratum (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.30-0.54), not a pre-specified per-allele analysis, so the allele-specific benefit is inferred from the subgroup. Rank it on the registered OS endpoint; let the breakthrough flag describe the path, not the strength of evidence.

Ranking INCB161734 above GFH375 on line-fit is reasonable, but the efficacy under it is an uncontrolled n=41 phase 1 abstract at 2L+ (all >=2 prior lines), ORR 37% with no CI and mPFS/mDoR not reached at ~5 months (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.654). That is a response rate with no time-to-event anchor, which is exactly the surrogate I discount, and DAWN-303's front-line combination benefit is extrapolated across both line and setting. Keep it as an enrollable trial; do not let the 37% read as a durability estimate it does not carry.

We land on the same agent and the same n=500 randomized base, so this is a qualifier, not a fight. The grade >=3 table your safety-depth rank leans on (rash 14%, stomatitis 12%) is RASolute 302 (pmid:42223072), a 2L registration trial that RoB2 rates Some on open-label design, so the PFS and ORR read carry detection bias even where OS is largely insulated. That safety datum was characterized in pretreated patients, not the treatment-naive 79-year-old he is; the 1L read still sits with RASolute 303 (nct:NCT07491445), unposted. I also concede your point that the zoldonrasib allele match is genuine biology, not just a cleaner AE table.

target_intervention_label: HRS-4642 (KRAS G12D inhibitor) + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, first-line (phase 3 NCT07232875)
comment: Ranking the Hengrui HRS-4642 program at rank 2, ahead of daraxonrasib, puts a China-based front-line phase 3 that is not yet recruiting above the one agent on this axis with FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation and a positive randomized phase 3. NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 assigns no category to any KRAS G12D agent, so the tie-break is which trial a US patient can actually enter on the guideline-consonant path, and that favors the Western-sponsored RASolute slots. The 63.3% ORR is real but single-arm on a full gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone; I would not let it outrank the controlled evidence.

target_intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375, KRAS G12D-selective inhibitor + cetuximab, 1L cohort (NCT07644559)
comment: I share the driver logic, but leading with a China-based phase 1/2 (GFH375X1101) single-arm ORR over daraxonrasib inverts the evidence order that NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025's trial-enrollment frame would rank on. VS-7375 stays inside the guideline-consonant frame because it has a US-sponsor 1L cohort and an ESMO 2025 presentation, so it is a defensible pick, just not a defensible number-one over the phase-3-anchored option. The cetuximab pairing also adds a toxicity layer the RAS(ON) monotherapy trials do not carry for a 79-year-old.

Same lead, same reasoning. Under NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025 no KRAS G12D agent carries a consensus category, so among trial-enrollment options daraxonrasib is the one nearest a future listing: positive randomized phase 3 (RASolute 302, OS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo) plus FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation. Your planning-around-a-per-term-safety-table logic and my proximity-to-consensus logic converge here, which is the cross-frame agreement I weight most.

We land the same order, so this is a framing note rather than a disagreement. You rank zoldonrasib second on "biology over data" and flag the n=40 abstract as thin, which is fair on the numbers, but the guideline-consonant reason it belongs at rank 2 is concrete: RASolute 305 (NCT07621718) is a registered double-blind front-line phase 3 requiring KRAS G12D, so it is the correct design to settle the allele question rather than a mechanistic bet. NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025 gives no category to any of these, so a registered 1L phase 3 in progress is the strongest guideline-fit signal available short of a readout.

Agreed on rank 5 and the reason. There is no NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025 category for an ARID1A/ATR agent, and germline testing came back negative, which also closes the one DDR route that does carry a category here, the BRCA/PALB2 olaparib POLO maintenance line (NCCN category 2A). So the synthetic-lethal axis is a later-line, IHC-gated trial option with no PDAC responder, exactly as you place it, not a front-line contender.

target_intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375, oral KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor
comment: Serving prefers_trials does not by itself justify ranking VS-7375 above daraxonrasib, because both have open recruiting 1L slots, so the preference is satisfied either way and the tie-break falls to evidence strength. On that axis the guideline-consonant order under NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025 puts the FDA-breakthrough, randomized-phase-3 agent first and the China-based single-arm ORR second. A 41% response number one line removed from this patient is a weaker anchor than an OS hit, even for a trials-leaning patient.

target_intervention_label: ELI-002 2P, lymph-node-targeted amphiphile mKRAS peptide vaccine (G12D/G12R)
comment: Your HLA screen is right and worth keeping on the record: C*05:01/C*06:02 shuts out the C*08:02/A*11:01-restricted TCR-T and mRNA vaccine programs, and ELI-002 is the one HLA-agnostic construct left. My guideline-fit caveat is the setting. Its evidence sits in resected minimal-residual-disease PDAC, which is an adjuvant frame, so for bulky metastatic disease it is off the population the data support and belongs below every enrollable metastatic KRAS trial, roughly where you placed it.

Ranking the highest-ORR option second reads the number and not the man. HRS-4642 here is IV on a gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone that ran a 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE rate, and its phase 3 (nct:NCT07232875) is not yet recruiting, so it half-serves the one preference that carries weight, prefers_trials. For a 79-year-old the free_text already flags as likely toxicity-averse past the neutral 0.5, an IV chemo doublet at that grade-3 rate is the wrong front of the ranking.

target_intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375, oral KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor
comment: This is the top pick I share, and for the patient's reasons rather than the ORR alone. GFH375 is oral, matched to his exact G12D, and has an open recruiting 1L PDAC cohort (nct:NCT07644559), which lands prefers_trials, the driver, and the gentler-route instinct in one option. Grade >=3 TRAE sat at 30.3% (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099), well under the HRS-4642 backbone, so it also fits the toxicity-aversion the free_text warns 0.5 understates.

Keeping the 63.3% ORR off your top five on a 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE rate is the right call from the patient's side, and I will say so plainly. Even read as chemo-backbone toxicity, that grade-3 burden on an IV doublet is what a 79-year-old flagged as toxicity-averse would most want to avoid. You reached it on characterized-safety grounds and I reach it on preference_fit; either way the headline number does not earn a front-line slot for this man.

toxicity_vetoes is empty so I raise no veto, and your rank-2 for zoldonrasib is close to where the patient's toxicity lens points too: no grade 4 or 5 events, rash only 10% (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.4_suppl.724). My one qualifier is that the enrollable RASolute 305 slot (nct:NCT07621718) adds the agent to mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab-paclitaxel, so the clean monotherapy signal is not what he actually takes on; the combination toxicity at 79 is unpublished, and that belongs in front of him.

I keep daraxonrasib in my own top tier and your evidence-grade rank-1 is the anchor I want under any trials-forward recommendation to this patient: the only randomized OS result on his driver, HR 0.40 (pmid:42223072), with a recruiting front-line slot he qualifies for (nct:NCT07491445). It is oral too, which costs him nothing under a silent modality field and matters at 79. The one thing I carry past your read is prefers_trials does not separate it from the allele-matched agents, since GFH375 and zoldonrasib also recruit 1L, so the patient-facing tiebreak still runs through tolerability.

Ranking VS-7375 fourth on strength of controlled evidence is defensible, but from the patient's chair it does better than fourth: oral, exact-allele, ORR 41% (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099), with an open recruiting 1L cohort that lands prefers_trials directly (nct:NCT07644559). Worth separating two things you rightly kept apart, the C*08:02-restricted TCR-T and the A*11:01 programs are genuine HLA ineligibilities for his C*05:01/C*06:02 genotype, not preference conflicts, so leaving them off the ranking is correct and not a call I would reopen.
